title: They Believe 2020 Was Stolen. They Could Be in Charge of Elections in 2028
gist: Wired review of GOP attorney general candidates in Arizona, Georgia, Kansas, Michigan and Nevada who have promoted 2020 election-fraud claims or signaled willingness to relitigate 2020, with several races polling tied. The piece argues these offices will matter for the 2028 presidential election.

insights.claim: A WIRED review found GOP attorney general candidates in more than half a dozen states, including swing states, who have repeatedly expressed belief the 2020 election was stolen, and several say they would relitigate it if elected.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: These offices could shape certification and election-law enforcement in 2028.
insights.locator: A WIRED review has identified a slate of GOP attorney general candidates

insights.claim: State attorneys general serve as chief legal officers and a check on governors and the federal government, and have recently resisted Trump administration efforts to take control of elections, seize ballots and obtain voter rolls.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Control of AG offices determines whether state-level checks on federal election actions persist.
insights.locator: The role of attorney general in the administration and protection of elections

insights.claim: Chicago Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights counsel Christina Beeler says attorneys general must be dedicated to upholding the rule of law and election results.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
entities: Chicago Lawyers' Committee for Civil Rights
insights.so_what: Advocates frame AG races as rule-of-law stakes.

insights.claim: Arizona state senator Warren Petersen signed documents asking Congress to accept alternate electors for Trump, was central to the Cyber Ninjas Maricopa audit, which found Biden won by more votes than first thought and cost taxpayers millions, and polls tied with Democrat Kris Mayes.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: A tied Arizona AG race is a swing-state exposure for 2028 election administration.
insights.locator: Warren Petersen, an Arizona state senator

insights.claim: Petersen has promised an expanded Election Integrity Unit if elected, saying people will know the AG is serious as the Trump DOJ is.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Signals alignment between state AG offices and federal 2020 investigations.
insights.quote: People will know we’re serious about it
insights.locator: “People will know we’re serious about it,”

insights.claim: Georgia GOP nominee Brian Strickland called the FBI raid on Fulton County election offices a transparency measure, said Fulton County can't run elections, and is tied with Democrat Tanya Miller in an AJC poll.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Georgia AG alignment with federal 2020 probes in a competitive race.

insights.claim: Kansas AG Kris Kobach, a long-time promoter of voter-fraud claims, once claimed about 18,000 noncitizens were on Kansas voter rolls from research that initially found six possible cases, served on Trump's 'election integrity' commission, and is in a tight race with Democrat Chris Mann.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: An incumbent election-denier AG shows how the office has been used.
insights.locator: Unlike the other election deniers on this list

insights.claim: Michigan GOP nominee Doug Lloyd, not usually labeled an election denier, told a podcast the AG could use investigators or Michigan State Police to look back at 2020 items, and polls tied with Democrat Eli Savit.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Even moderates signal willingness to reopen 2020 in a tied swing-state race.

insights.claim: Trump-endorsed Nevada candidate Adriana Guzmán Fralick would push a SAVE Nevada Act requiring passport or birth certificate proof, which experts say would disenfranchise millions, and trails Democrat Nicole Cannizzaro by 8 points.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Nevada is the one race here where the denier-aligned candidate trails.
